title: US v. Google ad-tech — redaction-motion deadline on the sealed remedies opinion (E.D. Va.)
source: NEWS: the 14-day redaction deadline in Judge Leonie M. Brinkema's 2026-09-02 remedies order, United States et al v. Google LLC, No. 1:23-cv-00108 (E.D. Va.), reported by four independent outlets fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200): ppc.land 'DOJ loses AdX divestiture bid as Brinkema accepts behavioral remedies', which quotes the order verbatim — 'Within 14 days, the parties must move for any redactions to the Memorandum Opinion' — and states both branches, 'if no redaction motions are filed the opinion is unsealed automatically' and 'if redactions are requested and approved by the court the opinion stays under seal and a redacted version is filed publicly'; ppc.land 'Judge spares Google's ad exchange and rewrites its auction rules instead' ('Her written opinion is sealed for fourteen days while both sides review it for confidential material'); techcrunch.com 2026-09-02 ('will remain under seal for 14 days to allow those involved to issue necessary redactions'); and aljazeera.com 2026-09-02 ('Brinkema filed her opinion under seal for 14 days'). 2026-09-02 + 14 days = 2026-09-16, reproduced by arithmetic rather than taken from any outlet's own restatement. The underlying docket entry was NOT fetched — courtlistener.com/docket/66753787 returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch this session, as did law.justia.com and concurrences.com, all recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked. Stays `estimate` on two counts that are not date doubt: the confirmed-prefix table in market-events-data.ts defines NO confirmed prefix for a federal court docket (the same schema gap ftc-v-amazon-antitrust-trial-2027-03-29 documented), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: Canonical file written by this event's own initial research, 2026-09-08, from the single proposal that existed (proposals/google-adtech-opinion-unseal-2026-09-16.from-goog-2026-10-28-print.json, 2026-09-08). Tier `low` is KEPT and now has a measurement behind it rather than a judgment: the nearest same-name comparable for a PROCESS day is the 2023-09-12 search-trial opening at -0.10% excess vs QQQ, and this case's own adverse LIABILITY verdict (2025-04-17) cost only -1.36% excess in one session, against +8.23% for the one day that was a REMEDY DECISION (2025-09-03, search case). 2026-09-16 is a process day. One framing the proposal carried is CORRECTED here, in the direction of less drama: the fork is not publish-vs-nothing. Per the order's own reported text the reasoning becomes public in BOTH branches — unsealed whole if nobody moves, or filed as a public redacted version if the court grants a motion — so the fork decides completeness and timing, not existence, and the operative terms are backstopped 16 days later by the jointly proposed Final Judgment (google-adtech-final-judgment-2026-10-02). The substance is also already reported: first look and last look prohibited, unified pricing rules deprecated, AdX real-time bid data shared with rival ad servers, equal latency and data signals (ppc.land, 2026-09-02). What is sealed is the REASONING. Two collisions make the date structurally unmeasurable rather than merely quiet: 2026-09-16 is FOMC decision day (fomc-2026-09-16, `confirmed`, 14:00 ET, a converged coin flip at ~52-59% hike as of 09-08) with retail sales and import/export prices at 08:30, NAHB HMI at 10:00 and the VIX AM settlement ~09:00 — no single-name attribution survives that tape. And it sits 10 sessions before the goog-2026-10-28-print D-20 entry close (2026-09-30), which is the one useful thing about it: the last scheduled ad-tech checkpoint while that pre-print long is still unopened rather than running. Both sides signalled appeal on day one (Google 'will appeal the underlying liability ruling'; DOJ 'evaluating appropriate next steps' — Al Jazeera, 2026-09-02), so neither this date nor 10-02 retires the overhang.
